title: The 120-day line

hook.main: Renewing by spring? Board before Dec 9.
hook.spoken: Renewing your mortgage by next spring? Your route runs through December 9th.

alts.onScreen: Mark Dec 9 on your renewal route.
alts.spoken: Mark December 9th on your renewal route, even if your mortgage matures in March.

alts.onScreen: Waiting for the letter costs you time.
alts.spoken: The renewal mistake is waiting for the letter. It only has to arrive 21 days before your term ends.

angle: Edmonton renewers maturing between now and spring 2027 face two moving parts before they sign: the Bank of Canada's Dec 9 decision (prime, variable payments) and bond yields (fixed rates). The renewal is drawn as one printed transit line from TODAY to MATURITY that crosses the North Saskatchewan River; the bank's letter is a station near the very end (day 21), the rate hold is the first station (up to 120 days), and at the Dec 9 interchange the variable branch forks HIKE/HOLD while the held fixed line runs straight through. Edmonton's own number (benchmark $417,200, down 0.9% in a year, RAE Oct 2026) says the appraisal is unlikely to be the obstacle for most renewers here, so the calendar is the risk. Fills the 'nobody runs a Dec 9 countdown' gap in landscape_2026-11-19.
clientFacts: City: Edmonton (kit.json city) -> the line crosses a flat blue North Saskatchewan River band; Edmonton numbers only, per kit rule r1
Brokerage and people: Keith Crosland & Dustin Moss, Mortgage Connection (kit.json brokerage, people) printed in the map's cartouche on the payoff beat
Local market: RAE Oct 2026 MLS HPI composite benchmark $417,200, -0.9% y/y (sourced, dated)
styleWhy: Transit Map's native move is a line that exists only as far as its pen tip has travelled and an interchange that lands with weight when a second line arrives, which is exactly this story: a 120-day route you board early, with Dec 9 as the junction where the variable branch splits.
rejectedStyles: countdown (a launch clock has no route, so the day-21 letter station and the fork are lost)
pictogram-motion (signs and objects, but no single journey to ride)
device: One printed metro-map sheet on a dark table, laid out for 9:16: the Renewal Line runs top (TODAY) to bottom (MATURITY) with day-stops; a flat blue river band crosses mid-sheet; station 'DAY 21: BANK'S LETTER' sits two stops from the end; at the 'DEC 9' interchange the variable branch forks into HIKE and HOLD while the held-fixed line runs straight; a small mechanical counter printed on the sheet counts days to Dec 9.
mechanic: Countdown tracker plus find-your-station: the on-sheet counter shows days to Dec 9 from the posting date, and a pause beat asks viewers to find their maturity month (JAN / FEB / MAR stations in big type) and count back 120 days to their boarding date.
structure: Callout + deadline, then problem (letter comes late) -> solution (board early with a hold) -> twist (Dec 9 fork) -> personal action (find your station) -> loop to the counter. 45 s.

beats.visual: Low macro on the paper; a glowing pen tip lights the TODAY stop and the mechanical counter clacks to the days-to-Dec-9 number (20 if posted Nov 19).
beats.text: Renewing by spring? Board before Dec 9.
beats.voice: Renewing your mortgage by next spring? Your route runs through December 9th.

beats.visual: Camera pulls back to show the whole line; far down, one station prints in red: DAY 21: BANK'S LETTER, two stops from MATURITY.
beats.text: The letter can come 21 days out
beats.voice: But your lender only has to send the renewal letter 21 days before your term ends.

beats.visual: The pen tip races back up to the top; first station after TODAY lights: RATE HOLD, up to 120 days. A ticket stub prints beside it.
beats.voice: So board early. Many lenders will hold a rate for up to 120 days.

beats.visual: The line dives under the flat blue river band (North Saskatchewan, unlabelled river shape); station APPRAISAL prints a note: Edmonton benchmark $417,200, down 0.9% in a year (RAE, Oct 2026).
beats.voice: Edmonton values barely moved this year, so the appraisal should hold up. The calendar is the real risk.

beats.visual: DEC 9 interchange lands with weight; the variable branch forks: HIKE (+$39/mo on a $300,000 variable, illustrative) and HOLD (+$0). Counter visible in the corner.
beats.voice: On December 9th the Bank of Canada decides. A hike adds about thirty-nine dollars a month on a three-hundred-thousand variable.

beats.visual: The held fixed line runs straight under the junction, untouched; its ticket stub reads HELD 4.44% (insured 5-yr fixed, nesto, Nov 19, illustrative).
beats.voice: Fixed rates follow bond yields, any day. A hold keeps today's fixed offer, whichever branch wins.

beats.visual: Camera glides down to three big stations, JAN, FEB, MAR; a dotted guide counts back 120 days from MAR to a boarding stop near TODAY. Pause cue.
beats.voice: Find your maturity month on the line and count back 120 days. That's your boarding date.

beats.visual: Pull up to TODAY; the cartouche prints 'Keith Crosland & Dustin Moss · Mortgage Connection · Edmonton' + compliance placeholder; the counter clacks one day down and the frame matches frame 1 (loop).
beats.text: Save this. Set your boarding date.
beats.voice: Save this, and set a reminder for your boarding date.

title: Same wall, different renewal

hook.main: Same wall, same mortgage. Guess the gap.
hook.spoken: Two Edmonton neighbours share one wall and the same mortgage. Five years from now, one has paid a lot more. Guess how much.

alts.spoken: About eighty dollars a month. That's the gap between two neighbours with the same mortgage.
Illustrative example: two neighbours in an Edmonton semi got their renewal letters the same week. Only one opened it.

angle: One Edmonton semi-detached house (the one home type whose sales rose a lot this October: +12.4% y/y, average $410,683, RAE) split down its party wall into two labelled composite households with identical mortgages. Left signs the first renewal offer when the letter lands; right starts 120 days early and shops. A guess-then-reveal turns a 0.50% illustrative rate gap into roughly $7,000 of extra interest over five years. Keith and Dustin's real background (both spent years inside big banks) gives the bridge line credibility without inventing a testimonial.
clientFacts: City: Edmonton (kit.json); house type and price from RAE Oct 2026 Edmonton semi-detached data
Background: Keith Crosland, banking since 2008 with ten years as a mortgage specialist; Dustin Moss, 14+ years at a Big 5 bank, last seven in mortgages (kit.json bio, staff pages)
Brokerage: Mortgage Connection (kit.json brokerage) on the name plate at the payoff
styleWhy: Halftone Dossier reads a file out one exhibit at a time with stamps that slam, so 'left signed, right shopped' becomes two rubber stamps on the same case file and the guess-then-reveal gets a natural freeze before the verdict stamp.
rejectedStyles: stick-explainer (good for before/after, but loses the bureaucratic paper-and-stamp joke that carries the renewal letter)
pop-art (one-number punch only; no exhibit structure for a two-household comparison)
device: A cream case file on one Edmonton semi-detached house drawn in halftone, split by a red line down the party wall; the left and right halves are two faceless composite households labelled 'Illustrative example'; numbered exhibits (A: same mortgage, B: the letter, C: the rate cards) compare sides; stamps SIGNED (left, day 21) and SHOPPED (right, day 120); a fat halftone counter spins during the guess freeze and stops on the verdict.
mechanic: Guess-then-reveal: a 2-second freeze with a spinning counter and 'Your guess?' before the verdict stamp; the payoff line is a send built into the story ('send this to your neighbour').
structure: Same X, different outcome; before-after-bridge. Setup (same house, same mortgage) -> split (sign vs shop) -> monthly gap -> guess freeze -> verdict -> bridge to the brokers -> send. 45 s.

beats.visual: Case file slams onto the frame: a huge halftone semi-detached house, a red line drops down the party wall. File chip: EDMONTON SEMI · avg $410,683 (RAE, Oct 2026).
beats.text: Same wall, same mortgage. Guess the gap.
beats.voice: Two Edmonton neighbours share one wall and the same mortgage.

beats.visual: EXHIBIT A stamps across both halves: $300,000 left · 20 years · renewing 2027. Small label: Illustrative example.
beats.voice: Five years from now, one of them has paid a lot more. Guess how much.

beats.visual: EXHIBIT B: the renewal letter drops into the left mailbox, a calendar chip reads DAY 21; a hand signs; red stamp SIGNED.
beats.voice: The left side gets the renewal letter three weeks out, and signs it.

beats.visual: Right half: calendar chip DAY 120, a phone, two lender cards fan out; stamp SHOPPED in the highlight ink.
beats.voice: The right side starts four months early, and shops the same mortgage.

beats.visual: EXHIBIT C: two rate cards pinned either side of the wall: 4.94% vs 4.44% (illustrative; 4.44% = insured 5-yr fixed, nesto, Nov 19).
beats.voice: Say the first offer sits half a point above a shopped rate.

beats.visual: Payments print under each half: $1,962 vs $1,882; an $80 slug slides through the wall from right to left.
beats.voice: That's about eighty dollars a month.

beats.visual: Freeze: the halftone counter spins over the wall, 'Your guess?' in the hand face; 2-second hold with a ticking sting.
beats.voice: Over five years?

beats.visual: Verdict stamp slams over the left half: $7,032 MORE INTEREST; footnote with assumptions.
beats.voice: About seven thousand dollars more in interest, for the same house.

beats.visual: Name plate slides in at the foot of the file: Keith Crosland & Dustin Moss · Mortgage Connection · Edmonton + compliance placeholder; camera pulls back to the whole split house (matches frame 1, loop).
beats.voice: We both spent years at big banks. The first offer is where the talk starts. Send this to the neighbour renewing next.

title: Some assembly required: three bills, one renewal

hook.spoken: We ran the numbers on an Edmonton renewal with thirty-five thousand dollars of card and car debt sitting beside it.

alts.spoken: About six hundred and forty dollars a month. That's what folding two debts into one renewal changed in our example.
The renewal mistake: signing a straight renewal while a 21% card balance sits right next to it.

angle: Renewal is the one moment a closed mortgage can be restructured without a break penalty, which makes it the natural window for Keith and Dustin's refinancing and debt-consolidation work. The Edmonton number does real work: a refinance can borrow up to 80% of value, and on Edmonton's benchmark home ($417,200, RAE Oct 2026) that ceiling is $333,760, so a $330,000 combined mortgage just fits. The honest turn (you re-qualify at rate + 2%, and stretching a car loan over 20 years costs interest) leads to a payoff that saves money for real: keep paying the old total and the whole balance could be gone years sooner.
clientFacts: City: Edmonton (kit.json); 80% ceiling computed on the RAE Oct 2026 Edmonton benchmark $417,200
Services: Refinancing, Second Mortgages, Alternative Lending (kit.json services) and Debt consolidation (kit.json audience/specialties)
Brokerage: Keith Crosland & Dustin Moss, Mortgage Connection on the last manual page
styleWhy: Instruction Manual Art's native move is assembling separate parts into one, with yellow marking the new part, a parts box with counts and a do/don't box, so three loose bills clicking into one yellow mortgage block, with a caution sign before the final step, is the style doing what it was built for.
rejectedStyles: assembly-line-diagram (a conveyor reads as a factory process, not a household decision)
iso-infographic (coloured diorama and data panels, colder and busier on a phone)
device: One printed flat-pack manual page in true isometric: a parts box lists 1x mortgage block ($295,000), 1x card ($15,000), 1x car loan ($20,000) with their monthly payments as counts; faceless hands fit them step by step; a magnifier circle on an isometric Edmonton house shows an 80% gauge ($333,760 of $417,200); a caution triangle before the last step; a do/don't box (check: keep paying the old total; cross: refill the card). Yellow appears only on the new combined mortgage, and late yellow carries the payoff.
mechanic: Comment keyword that delivers: 'Comment LIST' sends a one-page debt tally sheet (to be produced and approved before posting). Secondary: a pause beat invites viewers to count their own 'parts' against the parts box.
structure: I ran the numbers -> parts (three bills) -> rule (renewal = no break penalty) -> Edmonton 80% ceiling -> assembly (one payment) -> caution (re-qualify, longer debt) -> do/don't payoff -> comment keyword; loop to the parts box. 46 s.

beats.visual: Parts box slides onto the page: three white parts with labels in numbers only: $295,000 · $15,000 · $20,000. Hands rest beside them.
beats.voice: We ran the numbers on an Edmonton renewal with thirty-five thousand dollars of card and car debt.

beats.visual: STEP 1: each part shows its monthly count: $1,850 · $450 · $498; a dotted guide sums them: $2,798.
beats.voice: Three bills, about twenty-eight hundred dollars a month.

beats.visual: STEP 2: magnifier circle over a calendar part: renewal date, a crossed-out penalty icon.
beats.voice: But at renewal you can restructure without a break penalty.

beats.visual: STEP 3: isometric Edmonton house with a gauge strip: $417,200 x 80% = $333,760; a $330,000 marker slides in just under the line.
beats.voice: A refinance can borrow up to 80 percent of value. On Edmonton's benchmark home, that's about three-thirty-four thousand.

beats.visual: STEP 4: the three parts click into one block that turns safety yellow: $330,000 · 4.95% · 20 yrs = $2,160/mo. 'Click' mark.
beats.voice: Fold it into one mortgage and the bill drops to about twenty-one sixty, roughly six-forty less.

beats.visual: Caution triangle page: 'Re-qualify at 6.95%' and a car part stretched along a 20-year rule.
beats.voice: Therefore you re-qualify at your rate plus two. And a car loan over twenty years costs more interest.

beats.visual: Do/don't box: check (blue) = hand keeps paying $2,798 into the yellow block, a counter shows ~13 years instead of 20; cross (red) = card part refilling.
beats.voice: So keep paying the old total, if your prepayment terms allow, and it could be gone about six years sooner.

beats.visual: Last page: hands close the manual; footer prints Keith Crosland & Dustin Moss · Mortgage Connection · Edmonton + compliance placeholder; the parts box reopens (loop).
beats.text: Comment LIST for our debt sheet
beats.voice: Comment LIST for the one-page sheet we use to tally debts before a renewal.

cta: comment keyword: 'Comment LIST and we'll send the one-page sheet we use to tally debts before a renewal.' (delivers a real sheet; see needs)
sendTest: Someone in Edmonton renewing in 2027 with holiday card debt sends it to their partner before they talk about the renewal letter.

math.working: Mortgage renewed: $295,000, 20 yrs, 4.44% insured (nesto Nov 19), semi-annual compounding = $1,850.35; card $15,000 x 3% minimum = $450.00; car loan $20,000, 48 months, 8.99% = $497.61; total $2,797.95
$330,000, 20 yrs, 4.95% uninsured (refinances are uninsured; nesto Nov 19) = $2,159.61; $2,797.95 - $2,159.61 = $638.34
Stress test = higher of contract rate + 2% (4.95% + 2% = 6.95%) or 5.25%

math.claim: Car/card portion over 20 years costs more interest
math.result: about $20,000 of interest if only minimums are paid on the combined loan

math.claim: Keep paying the old total: about 13 years instead of 20
math.result: about six years sooner (conditional on prepayment privileges; a 30% payment increase exceeds some lenders' limits)
